Settings.LanguageNotRemembered: The language is changed for now, but it could not be saved, so the next start uses the previous one.
Settings.Title: Settings
Settings.DifferentVaultIntro: Point the application at a vault file kept somewhere else — a copy on a memory stick, a synced folder, a file carried over from another machine. Because the vault file is portable, the copy opens exactly like the original.
Settings.DifferentVaultDeviceUnlock: A vault opened from a different path has no device unlock of its own: "remember on this device" is tied to the exact path a vault was opened from, so it always asks for the master password the first time, even if this switch is on below for the vault at the path above.
Settings.RememberIntro: Tied to the path above: renaming or moving the vault file asks for the master password once, even with this switched on.
Settings.NodeUrlsIntro: Which rippled node each network publishes to and reads from. Pick one of the listed servers, or “Built-in” to use the endpoint this application ships with for that network; “Custom URL” takes any {ws} or {wss} address. A network this application does not already know — a NetworkID, or a private stand — needs a URL here before anything can be published to it.
Settings.AddNetworkLabel: Add a network not listed above
Settings.AddNetworkHint: A locally run standalone node, for one: its network is a NetworkID such as {example}, which has no row until it is added here.
Settings.NodeNotANetwork: '{network}' is not a network an xrpl-file link can name.
Settings.NodeUrlMissing: Give the new network a URL to save it with.
Settings.NodeUrlNotWebSocket: '{url}' is not a ws:// or wss:// URL.
Settings.NodeRowUrlNotWebSocket: '{url}' for {network} is not a ws:// or wss:// URL.
Vault.UnlockSuccessDetail: The password worked, and every entry checked out clean.
Vault.UnlockWrongPasswordDetail: That password does not open this vault. Check it and try again.
Vault.UnlockMissingDetail: There is nothing to open at this location yet.
Vault.UnlockCorruptDetail: The vault's record did not check out. Whether the password was wrong or the file itself is damaged cannot be told apart from here, so neither is assumed.
Vault.UnlockDegradedDetail: The password worked. Some entries inside failed their own integrity check and are listed as damaged; the rest are unaffected and still work.
Vault.UnlockUnsupportedDetail: This build does not understand the format this vault was written in.
Vault.UnlockUnavailableDetail: The vault's storage did not respond. This is usually temporary; try again in a moment.
Vault.CreateFirstRun: This is the first time this application has run here, and there is nothing to open yet.
Vault.CreateNoRecoveryBody: The master password you choose below is the only way this vault will ever open. If it is forgotten, every key inside that was not individually exported is gone for good — there is no support process, no reset link and no backdoor that gets it back.
Vault.CreateSuccessDetail: The vault is open and ready.
Vault.CreateExistsDetail: There is already a vault at this location. Creating a new one here would destroy every key inside it, so nothing was written.
Vault.CreateStorageDetail: The vault could not be written. Check that the location is writable and try again.
Vault.CreateTooShortDetail: The master password must be at least {minimum} characters. It is the only thing that will ever open this vault, and there is no recovery phrase behind it.
Vault.UnreachableLead: This application was pointed at a vault kept somewhere else, and nothing answered at that location just now. {notFresh} — a vault was chosen here before, and it is not offered to create a new one, because that would write a second, different vault at the remembered location and leave the real one wherever it actually is.
Vault.UnreachableNotFresh: This is not a fresh install
Vault.UnreachableCause: This usually means the medium holding it is not reachable right now — a memory stick not plugged in, a synced folder that has not caught up yet. Reconnect it and try again.
Vault.StartFreshBody: Forgetting this location does not touch the vault file itself — it only stops this application from looking for it here on its own. If the medium holding it reconnects later, point the application at it again from Settings. After forgetting, restarting opens (or offers to create) the vault at the default location instead.
Vault.ForgetLocationButton: Forget this location and start fresh
Vault.DamageIntro: These entries failed their own integrity check the last time the vault was opened. Everything else in the vault is unaffected and still works.
Vault.DamageWritesRefused: Adding, exporting or deleting keys is refused until this has been acknowledged. The record above is the only witness there is to what was lost — look at it before pressing the button below, because acknowledging clears the block, not the fact that it happened.
Vault.CurrentPasswordWrong: The current password is wrong. Nothing was changed.
Vault.ChangeTooShort: Choose a new password of at least {minimum} characters. Nothing was changed, and the current password still opens the vault.
Vault.ChangeDeviceUnlockDropped: "Remember on this device" could not be carried over to the new password and has been turned off. Turn it back on if you still want it.
Vault.ChangeOldCopyRemains: A copy of the vault from before this change is still at {path}, and the old password still opens it. Delete it once the new file is confirmed working, and treat the old password as compromised until then.
Vault.ChangeIntegrityRepaired: The vault's record did not match its own integrity code before this change. It has been repaired as part of the change, but this was the only chance to learn that — check your keys for anything missing or unexpected.
Vault.ErrorCorrupt: The vault's record did not check out and could not be read.
Vault.ErrorUnsupported: This build does not understand the vault's format.
Vault.ErrorLocked: The vault is locked. Unlock it and try again.
Vault.ErrorNoSuchEntry: That key is no longer in the vault.
Vault.ErrorDuplicateAddress: The vault already holds this address on this network.
Vault.ErrorEntryDamaged: This entry is damaged and cannot be read.
Vault.ErrorStorageFailed: The vault's storage did not respond. Try again in a moment.
Vault.ErrorDegraded: The vault found damage that has not been acknowledged yet. Acknowledge it first.
Vault.ErrorAddressMismatch: This entry's recorded address does not match its own key.
Vault.DeviceUnlockNotCreated: This device could not create a secret to remember the vault with, so it will keep asking for the master password. Nothing about the vault has changed.
Vault.LocationNotSaved: This choice could not be saved, so the application will still open the vault it opens now. The folder holding its settings may be read-only or full.
Vault.LocationSaved: Saved. Restart the application to open the vault at the new location.
Vault.LocationNotForgotten: This location could not be forgotten, so the application will still look for the vault here. The folder holding its settings may be read-only. The vault file itself has not been touched.
Vault.LocationForgotten: Forgotten. Restart the application to start fresh at the default location.
Shell.ScreenFailed: This screen stopped because of an error. Choose a tab to carry on.
Network.NotANetwork: '{network}' is not a network an xrpl-file link can name. Use mainnet, testnet, devnet, or a network ID in digits.
Accounts.Title: Accounts
Accounts.PublishingDescription: Throwaway accounts this app created for publishing. Close one to delete it from the ledger and get its reserve back.
Accounts.KeysDescription: Accounts you imported to sign publications. Close one only if you no longer need it on the ledger.
Accounts.NotExportedHint: This key exists only in this vault. Export it to keep a copy.
Accounts.DeleteIntro: This removes the key for {address} from this vault. The account on the ledger is not touched.
Accounts.DeleteNeverExported: This key has never been exported. Nothing else holds its secret, so deleting it loses access to that account for good.
Accounts.ReadFailed: The node did not answer, so the balance could not be read. Check the node URL in Settings, then choose Check balance from the account's menu to try again.
Accounts.NewIntro: This generates a key, not an account — on the XRP Ledger an account exists once it holds its reserve, so the account appears on the ledger only once somebody funds the address it gets.
Accounts.NewNeedsLabel: Give the account a name, so you can tell it from the others later.
Funding.Title: Fund this account
Funding.InstructionAccountExists: Send XRP to the address below, from any wallet.
Funding.InstructionAccountMissing: Send XRP to the address below, from any wallet. The account appears on the ledger once it holds its reserve.
Close.Title: Close account
Close.ImportedWarning: This is an imported key. Closing deletes its account from the ledger for good — make sure it is not an account you still use.
Close.Intro: Closing sends everything this account holds to a destination you choose.
Close.IntroWarning: The account will cease to exist, and this cannot be undone.
Close.ConfirmSend: This will send everything this account holds to {destination}, which currently holds {balance}.
Close.ConfirmWarning: The account will cease to exist once this is sent. This cannot be undone.
Close.NotYetLedger: It cannot be closed yet. It becomes possible from ledger {ledger}.
Close.ChooseDestination: Choose where the remainder should go.
Close.AnotherAccountClosing: Another account is being closed. Wait until that has finished, then close this one.
Close.Interrupted: The close was interrupted before it could be confirmed either way. Press Check again before retrying — the account may already have been closed.
Close.RecordNotSaved: {outcome} The record of it could not be saved to the vault. Its transaction hash is {hash} — look the deletion up with that.
Close.RefusedFeeClaimed: The node refused the deletion. The attempt still claimed the fee — one owner reserve.
Close.RefusedNothingCharged: The node refused the deletion. Nothing was charged.
Close.OutcomeReady: This account can be closed now.
Close.OutcomeNotYet: This account cannot be closed yet. The ledger refuses to delete an account until 255 ledgers have closed since its last transaction, and it must hold enough to cover the fee.
Close.OutcomeDestinationMissing: There is no such account on this network, and the remainder would have nowhere to go. Check the address.
Close.OutcomeDestinationRefuses: That destination will not accept this payment: it is the account being closed, it requires a destination tag, or it only accepts senders it has authorised. Send the remainder somewhere else.
Close.OutcomeSubmitted: The account was closed and its remainder is on its way.
Close.OutcomeQueued: The node queued the deletion rather than applying it. Until a ledger takes it the account still exists and still holds everything, so check again in a moment.
Keys.ExportReminder: This key exists nowhere but this vault until it is exported.
Keys.BackupPasswordOptionalLabel: Backup password (leave blank if it has none)
Keys.InvalidSeed: That does not look like a valid seed.
Keys.KeyNoLongerAvailable: That key is no longer available. Open the backup again.
Keys.BackupKeyInvalidSeed: This key inside the backup does not look like a valid seed.
Keys.ContainerAddressMismatch: This key does not belong to the address the backup lists for it, so it was not imported.
Keys.ContainerRegularKey: This key signs for its account as a regular key. Only an account's own master key can be imported here.
Keys.BackupNotOurs: This file is not a backup this application can open.
Keys.BackupWrongPassword: That password does not open this backup.
Keys.BackupPasswordless: This backup carries no password of its own and cannot be imported from a file.
Keys.BackupIterations: This backup's parameters are outside what this build accepts.
Keys.BackupUnreadable: This backup could not be opened.
Keys.StoreLocked: Unlock the vault before adding a key.
Keys.StoreFailed: The key could not be stored.
Keys.ExportIntro: Exporting writes a portable backup file, protected by its own password — separate from the vault's master password. Anyone who has both the file (or the code below) and this password can spend from this account.
Keys.BackupCreated: Backup created. It is not saved anywhere yet — save it to a file, or scan the code, before leaving this screen.
Keys.QrTooLarge: This key's backup is too large for a single QR code. Use the file instead — splitting a backup across several codes is not supported.
Keys.BackupPasswordTooShort: Choose a backup password of at least {minimum} characters. This file is the only way back to this key if the master password is ever forgotten, and anyone who finds it can guess at it for as long as they like.
Keys.BackupSavedNotRecorded: The backup was saved, but the vault could not record that it was: {reason}
Keys.BackupNotWritten: The backup could not be written where you chose. Nothing was saved, and this key still exists only in this vault. Try somewhere with room to write.
Keys.RevealWarning: Anyone who sees this can spend from this account. It hides itself automatically after a minute, or the instant the vault locks.
Publish.ErrorNodeUnreachable: The node did not answer. Nothing was spent. Check the node URL in Settings and try again.
Publish.ErrorInsufficientBalance: The account does not hold enough to cover this publication. Fund it, or publish a smaller file.
Publish.ErrorSubmitRefused: The node refused a transaction. Neither funding the account nor retrying will change that on its own.
Publish.ErrorBudgetExceeded: The run would have cost more than it was started with, so it was stopped rather than allowed to overspend.
Publish.ErrorFeeMismatch: The node's price changed between the estimate and the run. Take a fresh estimate and start again.
Publish.ErrorValidationTimeout: Transactions were submitted but not seen validated in time. The run is listed under unfinished runs, and resuming does not pay again for the chunks and block lists that already landed.
Publish.ErrorResumeMismatch: This is not the file, or not the key, that the interrupted run started with.
Publish.ErrorSessionAlreadyRun: A publication session was run twice. That is a defect in this application, not something you did.
Publish.ErrorTooLarge: This application publishes files up to 16 GiB.
Publish.ErrorInvalidLink: The link is not a valid xrpl-file link.
Publish.ErrorManifestNotFound: The node has no manifest at that transaction hash.
Publish.ErrorNodeLacksHistory: The node does not keep history far enough back to read this file.
Publish.ErrorCorruptManifest: The manifest read back from the ledger is not one this version understands.
Publish.ErrorListMismatch: A block list read back from the ledger does not match what was written.
Publish.ErrorBlockMismatch: A block read back from the ledger does not match what was written. The manifest was not published, so no link points at it.
Publish.ErrorChunkMissing: A chunk that was written could not be read back from the ledger.
Publish.ErrorBatchNotEnabled: This network does not enable Batch. Choose Nobody under Paid by to publish with tickets.
Publish.ErrorPayerInsufficientBalance: The payer does not hold enough XRP for this publication. Fund it, or choose another payer.
Publish.ErrorAccountInUseWriterOrPayer: The writer or payer account sent a transaction of its own during the publication. Is this key in use somewhere else? The run is listed under unfinished runs; resume it once nothing else uses the key.
Publish.ErrorAccountInUseWriter: The writer account sent a transaction of its own during the publication. Is this key in use somewhere else? The run is listed under unfinished runs; resume it once nothing else uses the key.
Publish.ErrorAccountInUsePayer: The payer account sent a transaction of its own during the publication. Is this key in use somewhere else? The run is listed under unfinished runs; resume it once nothing else uses the key.
Publish.ErrorFeeTooHigh: Network fees rose above what this publication was approved for. The run is listed under unfinished runs; resume it when fees are back down.
Publish.ErrorWriterWindowConflict: The writer account carries other data for this file's chunks — was it used for another publication while this one was interrupted? Publish this file again from a fresh writer key.
Publish.ErrorApprovalExceeded: Fees or balances changed since this was approved. Estimate it again.
Publish.ErrorManifestRejected: The manifest landed, but reading it back did not give this file's description, so its link must not be shared. Publish the file again from a fresh writer key.
Publish.ErrorFeeTooLargeForApplication: The node is quoting a price this application cannot use. Try a different node.
Publish.ErrorFeeTooHighNow: Network fees are above what this application publishes at right now. Try again when they are back down.
Publish.ErrorHistoryLagged: The node's history fell behind the publication, so what landed could not be confirmed. The run is listed under unfinished runs; resume it, or choose another node in Settings first.
Publish.ErrorPayerShortBeforeResuming: The payer does not hold enough XRP to finish this publication. Fund it, then resume.
Publish.ErrorBatchOffBeforeResuming: This network no longer enables Batch; the run can be resumed once it does.
Publish.ErrorNodeUnreachableBeforeResumi: The node did not answer. This attempt spent nothing, and the run is still listed under unfinished runs. Check the node URL in Settings and try again.
Publish.ErrorNodeUnreachableWhileReading: Every chunk of the file is in the ledger and paid for, but the node stopped answering while the app read the file back to check it, so the link has not been written yet. The run is listed under unfinished runs: resume it to check the file again and write the link. Resuming pays only for the link's own transaction.
Publish.ErrorNodeUnreachableWhileSubmitt: The node stopped answering partway through the run. Transactions sent before that may already be in the ledger and paid for. The run is listed under unfinished runs: check the node URL in Settings, then resume it. Resuming does not pay again for the chunks and block lists that already landed.

The node stopped answering partway through the run. Transactions sent before that may already be in the ledger and paid for, and tickets it reserved may be on this account, each holding {reserve} of owner reserve until a later publication from this account spends them or the account is closed. The run is listed under unfinished runs: check the node URL in Settings, then resume it. Resuming does not pay again for the chunks and block lists that already landed.
Publish.Title: Publish a file
Publish.NoAccounts: No account to publish from yet. Create one on the Accounts tab.
Publish.PayerNobodyNote: Slower, and holds up to 50 XRP of reserve while publishing.
Publish.PayerBatchUnavailable: This network does not support Batch, so publishing uses tickets.
Publish.PayerRequired: Choose a payer — files larger than 64 MiB publish through Batch.
Publish.ChooseKey: Choose the key that will publish it.
Publish.FileEmpty: That file is empty, and an empty file has nothing to publish.
Publish.FileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
Publish.FileDialogFailed: The file dialog could not be opened.
Publish.PayerKeyGone: The key chosen to pay is no longer in the vault.
Publish.NetworkNotLinkable: The key's network '{network}' is not one an xrpl-file link can name. xrpl-file links use 'mainnet', 'testnet', 'devnet', or a NetworkID written as digits.
Publish.NoNodeUrl: No node URL is known for the network '{network}'. Add one in Settings.
Estimate.Title: Estimate
Estimate.RowFeesRetried: Fees if every transaction is retried
Estimate.AccountReserveStays: The account reserve stays on the account until the account is closed.
Estimate.WriterFeesWorstCase: Writer fees in the worst case
Estimate.PayerFeesWorstCase: Payer fees in the worst case
Estimate.ConfirmationLabel: I understand the cost and the time
Estimate.NothingReady: Nothing is ready to publish. Go back and estimate the file again.
Estimate.TooSmallForBatch: Too small for Batch — the writer pays its few transactions itself.
Estimate.NoTicketRoom: This account already holds the {limit} tickets the XRP Ledger allows, none of them recognisably left by this application, so a file this size has nowhere to put its own. Publish a smaller file, which needs no tickets, or use another account.
Estimate.NotAffordable: This publication needs {required} and the account can spend {spendable}. Fund it, or publish a smaller file.
Estimate.NotAffordableMostReserve: This publication needs {required} and the account can spend {spendable}. Most of it is reserve that comes back as the publication finishes: {reserve} for tickets. Fund it, or publish a smaller file.
Estimate.NotAffordableSomeReserve: This publication needs {required} and the account can spend {spendable}. Some of it is reserve that comes back as the publication finishes: {reserve} for tickets. Fund it, or publish a smaller file.
Estimate.ShortfallWriter: The writer {name} needs {required} and can spend {spendable}.
Estimate.ShortfallPayer: The payer {name} needs {required} and can spend {spendable}.
Estimate.ShortfallBoth: The writer {writer} needs {writerRequired} and can spend {writerSpendable}. The payer {payer} needs {payerRequired} and can spend {payerSpendable}.
Run.Title: Publishing
Run.AwaitingConfirmation: Waiting for you to confirm the cost below.
Run.StageReadBack: Reading it back from the ledger
Run.StageFence: Waiting for earlier transactions to expire
Run.MidReadBack: reading it back from the ledger
Run.MidFence: waiting for earlier transactions to expire
Run.CloseConfirmPlain: "{name}" is still publishing. Closing now will stop the run; it can be resumed later. Close anyway?
Run.CloseConfirmTickets: "{name}" is still publishing. Closing now stops the run; it can be resumed later. The tickets it reserved stay on this account, each holding {reserve} of owner reserve, until a later publication from this account spends them or the account is closed. Close anyway?
Run.TicketsUnfinished: Releasing the leftover tickets on this account did not finish. Any it did not release stay on the account, each holding {reserve} of owner reserve, until a later publication from this account spends them or the account is closed.

Run.TicketsReleased.one: {count} leftover ticket was released, freeing its owner reserve.
Run.TicketsReleased.other: {count} leftover tickets were released, freeing their owner reserve.

Run.TicketsNoneReleased.one: {count} leftover ticket could not be released.
Run.TicketsNoneReleased.other: {count} leftover tickets could not be released.

Run.TicketsSomeReleased.one: {count} leftover ticket was released, but {locked} could not be.
Run.TicketsSomeReleased.other: {count} leftover tickets were released, but {locked} could not be.

Run.TicketsStay.one: It stays on this account, holding {reserve} of owner reserve, until a later publication from this account spends it or the account is closed.
Run.TicketsStay.other: They stay on this account, each holding {reserve} of owner reserve, until a later publication from this account spends them or the account is closed.

Run.StateNote: This run's progress file could not be updated, so it may still be listed under unfinished runs. The file is published; delete that entry rather than resume it, which would pay again for transactions the file no longer needs.
Run.ErrorSourceUnreadable: The file at {path} could not be read. Choose it again.
Run.ErrorSourceReadFailed: The file could not be read. Make it available and publish it again.
Run.ErrorSourceReadFailedAt: The file at {path} could not be read. Make it available and publish it again.
Run.ErrorSourceReadFailedResuming: The file could not be read while it was being published. Make it available again and resume the run.
Run.ErrorSourceReadFailedResumingAt: The file at {path} could not be read while it was being published. Make it available again and resume the run.
Run.ErrorSourceChanged: The file at {path} has changed since the run started. Choose the original file.
Run.ErrorSourceNotThisRun: That file is not the one this run was publishing.
Run.ErrorStateNotWritten: The publication's state could not be written to disk, so the run was stopped.
Run.ErrorStateUnreadable: This run's state file could not be read, so it cannot be resumed.
Run.ErrorUnexpected: Something went wrong that this application does not have a specific message for. The run was stopped.
Run.HistoryNotRecorded: The publication succeeded, but could not be recorded in your history.
Run.HistoryRecordFailed: The publication succeeded, but recording it in your history failed unexpectedly: {error}
Unfinished.Title: Unfinished runs
Unfinished.DeleteNote: Deleting does not undo what a run already spent — only finishing it, by resuming, does not pay those fees again.
Unfinished.TicketNote: Deleting a run leaves the tickets it reserved on this account, each holding an owner reserve, until a later publication from this account spends them or the account is closed.
Unfinished.RowUnreadable: This run's state file could not be read.
Unfinished.NotListed: This run is no longer listed under unfinished runs, so there is nothing to resume.
Unfinished.NothingToResumeFrom: This run's state file cannot be read, so there is nothing to resume from. It can be deleted.
Unfinished.PayerKeyGone: The key that paid for this run is no longer in the vault. Choose another payer on the same network to resume it.
Unfinished.ChoosePayer: Choose a payer on this run's network.
Unfinished.SourceGone: The file this run was publishing is no longer at {source}. Choose it again.
Unfinished.FileUnreadable: That file could not be read.

Unfinished.FileSizeDiffers.one: That file is {count} byte and this run was publishing {expected}. Resuming needs the same file the run started with.
Unfinished.FileSizeDiffers.other: That file is {count} bytes and this run was publishing {expected}. Resuming needs the same file the run started with.

Unfinished.DeleteFailed: That state file could not be deleted.
History.Title: Published files
History.Lede: Forgetting or clearing only changes this list on this device. Every file is already in the ledger, and any link you kept elsewhere still works.
History.Empty: Nothing published yet. Files you publish from this device appear here with their links.
History.ListUnreadable: The publications file could not be read, so this list is empty. The file has been left as it is.
History.ListNotWritten: The publications file could not be written. Your file is in the ledger and your link is safe, but this history could not be updated. Try again later.
History.ListReplaced: Your previous publications list could not be read, so it has been replaced. This publication is recorded, but earlier entries may be missing.
History.HeldBack: Some publications that finished earlier are not in this list yet, because it could not be updated. Their links are kept and are added when the application starts with a list it can read and write.
Read.Title: Read a file
Read.ErrorInvalidLink: That is not an xrpl-file link.
Read.ErrorManifestNotFound: This network has no transaction at that hash. The link may be wrong, or it may belong to a different network.
Read.ErrorNodeLacksHistory: This node's history does not reach back far enough to hold the file. A node that keeps more history can read it.
Read.ErrorCorruptManifest: There is something at that hash, but it is not a file description this version understands.
Read.ErrorListMismatch: The list of the file's blocks does not match what the file's own description says it should be. Nothing was saved.
Read.ErrorBlockMismatch: A block of the file does not match what the file's own description says it should be. Nothing was saved.
Read.ErrorChunkMissing: Part of the file is not in the ledger. Nothing was saved.
Read.ErrorTooLarge: This file is larger than this application will read.
Read.ErrorNodeUnreachable: The node did not answer. Check the node URL in Settings and try again.
Read.ErrorNotCausedByReading: Something went wrong that reading a file cannot cause. This is a defect in this application, not something you did.
Read.ErrorTemporaryWriteFailed: The file could not be written to a temporary location while it was being read.
Read.ErrorGeneric: Something went wrong that this application does not have a specific message for.
Read.ErrorSaveFailed: The file could not be opened to save, or could not be written to where you chose.
Read.ErrorSaveFailedGeneric: Something went wrong while saving that this application does not have a specific message for.
Read.NoNodeUrl: No node URL is known for the network '{network}'. Add one in Settings.
Tutorial.ListOfferIntro: Short tutorials show how to create an account, add and export a key, publish a file and read one by its link.
Tutorial.ListNotNowHint: You can open them again any time from {learn} in the menu.
Tutorial.BusyPublishing: A publication is running. Try again when it finishes.
Tutorial.BusyReading: A read is running. Try again when it finishes.
Tutorial.TopicRead: Read a file by its link
Tutorial.ShowCreateAccount: Show how to create an account
Tutorial.LookupFailedNote: This link could not be looked up. The message on the screen says why; you can still go on.
Tutorial.ReadFailedNote: The file could not be read. The message on the screen says why; you can still go on.
Tutorial.CreateAccountSectionBody: Files go out from throwaway accounts that this application creates for you. They live in this section.
Tutorial.CreateAccountNewButtonBody: Choose {newAccount} to add an account. The tutorial opens that screen when you continue.
Tutorial.CreateAccountFieldsBody: The name only helps you tell accounts apart. Testnet XRP is free practice; mainnet costs real XRP.
Tutorial.CreateAccountGenerateBody: Choose {generate} to make a new key in your vault. The account is not on the ledger yet.
Tutorial.CreateAccountFundBody: Send XRP to the address from any wallet; choose {fund} on the key's row to see it. The account appears once it holds its reserve.
Tutorial.CreateAccountDoneBody: Export the new key so a copy exists outside this vault. The tutorial on exporting a key shows how.
Tutorial.AddKeyImportButtonBody: Choose {importKey} to bring in a key made elsewhere. The tutorial opens that screen when you continue.
Tutorial.AddKeySeedBody: A seed is the key itself, so keep it private. Choose {preview} to see the address before anything is stored.
Tutorial.AddKeyBackupBody: Choose {backupTab}, then pick a backup file written by this application's export, with its password.
Tutorial.AddKeyDoneBody: Imported keys are listed with the rest of your keys and publish like any other.
Tutorial.ExportKeyRowTitle: A key kept in one place
Tutorial.ExportKeyRowBody: A key that was never exported exists only in this vault. The next steps show how to export it.
Tutorial.ExportKeyMenuBody: The row's actions menu holds {exportKey}. The tutorial opens the export screen for this row when you continue.
Tutorial.ExportKeyPasswordBody: The backup has its own password, separate from your master password. Choose {createBackup} to make it; the file and its password together open the key.
Tutorial.ExportKeyDoneBody: Use {saveToFile} or {showQr}, and keep the copy on a different disk from this vault.
Tutorial.ExportKeyNoKeyBody: This vault has no key yet. Create one with {newAccount} first, then come back.
Tutorial.PublishFileBody: Pick the file to publish here. Bigger files cost more.
Tutorial.PublishFromBody: This account writes the file to the ledger and is named in its link.
Tutorial.PublishPayerBody: Large files can be paid for by a second account. With "Nobody" it is slower and holds reserve while it runs. This choice appears only when it applies.
Tutorial.PublishEstimateBody: Choose {estimate} to see the cost and the time first. Nothing is spent until you start the run from that screen.
Tutorial.PublishHistoryBody: Every publication and its link are kept under {history}. A run that stopped is listed there as unfinished and resumes without paying twice.
Tutorial.PublishDoneBody: Pick a file, choose an account, check the estimate and start. When it finishes you get a link to the file.
Tutorial.ReadLinkRealBody: The box holds a sample link to a real file, the project logo. Choose {lookUp} to see what it points to.
Tutorial.ReadLinkShownBody: This is where you paste a link to a file. Choose {lookUp} to see its name, size and time to read.
Tutorial.ReadResultBody: The name, size and time to read appear here. Choose {read} to fetch the file.
Tutorial.ReadSaveBody: Choose {save} to put the file on your computer. It is optional, and reading needs no account and costs nothing.
Tutorial.ReadDoneBody: Any link you receive works the same way: paste it, look it up, read.
